messages:
sarah (Support): Heads-up — customer reported lots of failures from /v1/rerank around 09:12 UTC. Their error logs show repeated "invalid UTF-8" 400s and a couple of 502s. They included a sample request and say this started after a mobile release that added emoji reactions.

sarah (Support): Repro from them (sanitized):
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "show results for cafés and sushi 🍣",
  "candidates": [
    "cafe near me",
    "sushi places",
    "price range" ,
    "malformed\u0000string"
  ]
}
```
(note: they used a placeholder \u0000 in the sample; their raw logs show an actual NUL byte in the payload) :face_with_monocle:

sarah (Support): Customer says sometimes the API returns weird low ranking scores for otherwise similar candidates, but most urgent is the outright 400s/502s when emoji or non-latin chars present.

mike (eng-runtime): Thanks — pinging @anya & @kai. Initial thought: input validation in the gateway should detect non-UTF8 sequences and either reject with clearer error or sanitize. Do we have any current replacement strategy for NULs or surrogate pairs in rerank path? :eyes:

anya (eng-ml): We currently assume inputs are valid UTF-8 when tokenizing. A NUL (0x00) can break some C string handling in older tokenizers or in custom native helpers (we've seen this in past vectorization code). Also emojis with certain composition forms (ZWJ sequences) can change tokenization and sometimes trigger unexpected attention shapes, but that shouldn't cause a 502. 502s point to runtime errors / segfaults possibly in tokenization/native layer.

kai (devex): Repro attempt on my laptop with the customer's payload — I sent the payload with an explicit NUL bytes placeholder replaced by a real 0x00 and hit a deserialization error from the fronting gRPC->HTTP adapter:
```
ERROR: malformed request body: invalid UTF-8 sequence at offset 142
stack: grpc-adapter: parse_body -> stoi -> abort
```
I also tried sending emoji clusters (family ZWJ sequences) and they passed fine.

mike (eng-runtime): Ok that narrows it — gateway choking on NUL. Two asks:
1) Short term: return 400 with a clear message "control characters (U+0000) not allowed" instead of bubbling to 502.
2) Medium: sanitize by replacing U+0000 with U+FFFD or remove them before handing to tokenizer, maybe behind a flag.

anya (eng-ml): Agree. But note: replacing NULs can change ranking results. For customers relying on exact byte shapes for dedupe or similarity, replacement changes semantics. We should add telemetry to see how often replacements happen and provide an opt-in sanitize mode.

sarah (Support): Customer wants a timeline — they have production traffic degraded. Any chance of a quick patch?

mike (eng-runtime): I'll open a hotfix PR to the gateway that rejects control chars and logs a structured event. If tests pass we can ship a patch to canaries. @deploy-bot can you queue a canary once PR merges? :shipit:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for canary-13 (rerank-gateway-hotfix) — will start in ~5m.

kai (devex): I'll add a note in the JS/Python SDKs to pre-validate payloads on the client side and include a snippet:
```js
// sanitize user-provided strings before sending
function scrubNulls(s){ return s.replace(/\u0000/g, '\uFFFD'); }
```

anya (eng-ml): Also running a quick local fuzz on the tokenizer with NUL and many combined emoji forms — didn't crash the native tokenizer binary, so likely the issue is earlier in the HTTP/gRPC path where we use C libs that assume C-strings.

mike (eng-runtime): PR merged, tests OK. Canary started. Watching metrics: rerank-400-rate and rerank-502-rate, plus structured log event `invalid_control_char`.

mike (eng-runtime): Canary looks clean for 10m, 0 new 502s. Rolling to prod now.

deploy-bot: Rollout to prod started: rerank-gateway-hotfix -> 3 nodes at a time.

mike (eng-runtime): Prod rollout complete. Metrics: 400s for invalid control char increased (expected) and 502s dropped to baseline. I'll follow up with an RFC for optional server-side sanitization and telemetry (include per-customer opt-in).

kai (devex): Support KB draft ready: short guidance + SDK snippet and recommended customer message when they see these 400s. I'll push that to docs and link in the support ticket.

sarah (Support): Customer accepted temporary workaround (client-side scrub), flagged for follow-up on semantics changes. They asked if we can provide a list of exact characters we reject.

mike (eng-runtime): For now we explicitly reject the following control characters: U+0000 through U+001F, except common whitespace like \t \n. We'll document exact codepoints. Longer term we can make the list configurable per-tenant.

anya (eng-ml): Also note: if customers are sending binary blobs accidentally (attachments encoded inline), we should detect large non-printable sequences and return helpful errors.

sarah (Support): Great. I'll close the incident once KB is up and customer confirms. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

mike (eng-runtime): Filed follow-up RFC: RFC-1292 (sanitization + opt-in replacement). Assigned to @anya for ML considerations and @kai for SDKs.
